SEBoK Documentation and Records Management, Distilled

Fifth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 4/5. The prompt-named URLs Documentation_and_Records_Management and Documentation both 404; the discipline is dispersed across Information Management (SE-114), Technical Data Management (SE-124), Configuration Management (SE-047 / SE-097), and the surrounding records-and-archive surface. Editorial state reads as Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument with the §VII.7 anchor at IM (SE-114) for longitudinal-pulverization. The batch's three-carrier robustness stress-test (Doc 571 §X.5, Cluster E) lands here: documentation and records management is carried by three independent institutional carriers — ISO 15489 (records management), ISO/IEC/IEEE 26511-26515 family (technical documentation), and the configuration-management standard family (ISO 10007, EIA-649). The three carriers cross-map at the artifact-preservation rung. Cluster F longitudinal-pulverization at IM-anchor (SE-114, §VII.7-confirmed at three sub-rungs CM/TRA/DE) gains a fourth confirming sub-rung at records management proper. Cluster A universal-sibling at document-type and at retention-class composes; Cluster K V3 as records-discipline-binding (regulatory and forensic stakes force procedural binding) extends the §VII.6 V3-as-procedure-binding refinement.

II. Source Read

The discipline is dispersed. Information Management (SE-114) supplies the substrate-preservation discipline at the most general rung: capture, store, retrieve, archive, dispose, with provenance and integrity preserved across time. Technical Data Management (SE-124) supplies the engineering-artifact rung: drawings, specifications, models, test data, with the data-rights and ownership discipline. Configuration Management (SE-047 / SE-097) supplies the configuration-record discipline: baselines, change records, status accounting, audit trails. The carriers cross-map at the artifact-preservation rung. The three independent institutional carriers: ISO 15489 (records management family, retention schedules, evidential weight); ISO/IEC/IEEE 26511-26515 (documentation engineering, user docs, lifecycle docs); CM standards family (ISO 10007, EIA-649, MIL-HDBK-61). Document types span deliverable documentation, internal records, and contractual/regulatory records; retention is classed by regulatory horizon, business horizon, and disposable.

III. Structural Read

Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument, with three-carrier robustness (Cluster E) anchor stress-test. SE-186 is the batch's three-carrier robustness reading. The discipline lives across three independent institutional carriers (ISO 15489 records, IEEE 26511-family documentation, CM standards family) which cross-map at the artifact-preservation rung. This is convergent with SE-063 Measurement (PSM + GQM + ISO 15939) and SE-101 Medical Device (FDA Design Controls ↔ ISO 13485 ↔ ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288). The three-carrier sub-observation (Doc 571 §X.5) reaches a fourth load-bearing instance after SE-063, SE-112 System Security, SE-114 IM. SE-186 promotes three-carrier-robustness from formalization-strong to formalization-canonical at four anchored instances.

Cluster F longitudinal-pulverization (§VII.7 confirmed) at fourth sub-rung. SE-114 IM is the §VII.7 anchor for longitudinal-pulverization (Refinement D). §VII.7 confirmed three sub-rungs: CM/SE-097 (version-history), TRA/SE-141 (criterion-conformance trace), DE/SE-110 (integrated-state). SE-186 supplies a fourth sub-rung at records management proper — the records-retention discipline IS longitudinal-pulverization at the most general institutional rung (records preserved across decades for regulatory or forensic recall). The fourth sub-rung confirms the IM-anchor reassignment proposed at §VII.6 and reinforces records management as the canonical longitudinal-pulverization rung within IM's composition.

Cluster A universal-sibling lattice, two-axis (Doc 572 D.5.2). Document-type axis (deliverable, internal-record, regulatory-record) crosses retention-class axis (regulatory-horizon, business-horizon, disposable). Two-axis universal-sibling at the artifact rung; sixth load-bearing instance after SE-184. Two-axis sub-form is now formalization-canonical at six instances.

Cluster K V3-as-procedure-binding, records-discipline mode. Records management is V3-bound by regulatory and forensic stakes: the discipline cannot hold on archival virtue alone because evidential weight at audit or litigation forces procedural binding (chain-of-custody, retention schedules, disposition records). V3 sub-mode count: gate-binding (SE-185) plus a candidate seventh sub-mode at evidential-binding for records management. Convergent with SE-108 Safety's "procedure exists because virtue is structurally insufficient" reading at non-safety stakes (regulatory/forensic stakes are V3-binding-grade though not safety-grade).

Cluster H hypostatic-boundary, "the document IS the record." Records management asserts the artifact-as-record without claiming the artifact carries deeper substance: the record names what occurred, the discipline preserves the naming, no ontological claim is made about the recorded reality. Functional-surface discipline at the records rung.

V. Residuals

Editorial 404 confirms Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument at the documentation rung. The double 404 (Documentation_and_Records_Management and Documentation) is the editorial signal: SEBoK does not anchor the discipline because the institutional ecosystem (ISO 15489 + IEEE 26511 + CM standards) carries the formalization. Doubly-dispersed-but-internally-readable: the discipline can be reconstructed from SEBoK's surrounding surface composed with the external standards ecosystem.

VI. Provisional Refinements

Three-carrier robustness formalization-canonical at four anchored instances. SE-063, SE-112, SE-114, SE-186. Doc 571 §X.5 update warranted: three-carrier robustness is now a first-class Cluster E sub-form, no longer a candidate.

Cluster F Refinement D longitudinal-pulverization at IM-anchor: four sub-rungs confirmed. CM, TRA, DE, records management. The IM-anchor reassignment from CM (proposed §VII.6) is now load-bearing under four sub-rung evidence.

V3-as-procedure-binding evidential-binding sub-mode candidate. Records management's regulatory/forensic stakes force procedural binding at non-safety stakes. Worth tracking as a seventh sub-mode after gate-binding (SE-185).
